source.title: Handled, caller- or user-caused failures are logged with `logger.error` directly (unknown webhook, form-data length, polling triggers)

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

Several code paths catch an error that is caused by an external caller, the user's workflow, or a third-party API, handle it, and then log it with `logger.error` directly. They don't go through `ErrorReporter`, so the levels that n8n already gives errors (and the fix proposed in #43567) don't apply. A self-hosted instance that alerts on error-level logs gets alerted for things the operator cannot act on.

1. **Unknown webhook** — `packages/cli/src/webhooks/webhook-request-handler.ts`: when a `WebhookNotFoundError` is caught, it logs `Received request for unknown webhook: ...` at error and returns 404. The cause is a sender that still points at a deleted or deactivated workflow. On our instance, a Slack Events API subscription left behind after its workflow was deleted sent about 13,000 requests in 30 days, and our error-log alert fired almost every hour.
2. **Form-data length** — `packages/@n8n/backend-network/src/http/axios/utils.ts`: when `FormData.getLength` fails (e.g. a stream without a path in a multipart body of an HTTP Request node), it logs `Unable to calculate form data length` at error and sends the request without `content-length`. 16 of the 17 error-level lines on our instance over three days were this one.
3. **Polling triggers** — `GmailTrigger` (poll and simplify), `SalesforceTrigger`, `MicrosoftOneDriveTrigger`: in non-manual mode after the first poll, a failed API call is logged as `There was a problem in '<node>' node in workflow '<id>': ...` at error. Gmail swallows the error; Salesforce and OneDrive rethrow it, so the same failure is reported twice. Example: Gmail API `400 FAILED_PRECONDITION`.

The code is the same on `master` today.

A possible fix: log these at `warn`, or report them through `ErrorReporter` with the error's own level (`NodeApiError` / `NodeOperationError` already carry `level: 'warning'`), and keep `error` for issues the instance operator must act on. We run all three as patches on our instance. We'd like to check whether you'd accept this direction before opening a PR.

### To Reproduce

For 1:

1. `docker run -p 5678:5678 -e N8N_LOG_FORMAT=json n8nio/n8n:2.47.4`
2. `curl -X POST http://localhost:5678/webhook/does-not-exist`
3. See the container logs:

```
{"level":"error","message":"Received request for unknown webhook: The requested webhook \"POST does-not-exist\" is not registered.",...}
```

2 and 3 depend on the payload or the third-party API response, so we point to the code paths above instead of giving exact steps.

### Expected behavior

Requests to unknown webhooks, form-data length fallbacks, and API failures in polling triggers are logged at `warn`. Only issues the instance operator must act on are logged at `error`.

### Debug Info

Official Docker image `n8nio/n8n:2.47.4`, `N8N_LOG_FORMAT=json`, no Sentry DSN. Seen in production with PostgreSQL and task runners in external mode.

### Operating System

Docker Hardened Images / Alpine Linux v3.24 (official image)

### n8n Version

2.47.4

### Node.js Version

v26.13.0

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: grinem
comments.text:
Fully agree with this direction. Firing `error`-level logs on 404s/unknown webhooks and handled stream fallbacks breaks log-based alerting for self-hosted instances.

Downgrading `WebhookNotFoundError` to `warn` and the `FormData` length fallback to `debug`/`warn` is completely sane. For the polling triggers, delegating to `ErrorReporter` (or aligning on `NodeApiError` / `NodeOperationError` severity) makes a lot more sense than direct `logger.error` calls that cause duplicate reports.

If you open a PR, splitting the network/webhook log levels from the polling node refactor into separate commits (or PRs) will make it much faster for the core team to review and merge.
